full_judgment:
2. Mr Osman Ghani, learned Advocate for the petitioner, submits that the allegations disclosed in the petition of complaint are of civil nature and for the money involved in the petition of complaint the opposite party No.2, that is, Agrani Bank, Rangpur Cadet College branch, Rangpur by instituting Artha Rin Case No. 8 of 2002 got a decree for the said amount, as such, the instant proceeding if allowed to continue, that will perpetuate an injustice to the accused petitioner, as such, for ends of justice, the aforesaid case is liable to be quashed. 

 7. A proceeding can be quashed if on a reading of the complaint/first information report it appears that the allegations made in the petition of complaint/first information report does not in any way bring the accused petitioner within the ambit of the penal provision or the allegation made in the petition of complaint is barred by law or if it is of the opinion of the Court that if the petition of complaint be allowed to continue that will not bring any fruitful result to the complainant or the informant. On a reading of the complaint it appears that the offence/allegations made are relating to bank transaction and government for realising of bank transaction or default made in the bank transaction, promulgated Artha Rin Adalat Ain. It appears from Annexure C that-on the self-same averments made in the petition of complaint, the Bank has filed Artha Rin Adalat Case No. 8 of 2002 and obtained decree for the amount mentioned in the petition of complaint. It also appears from paragraph 8 of the complaint that the Bank has admitted that the accused petitioner has already made part payment of the said amount. Annexure F is the decree of the Artha Rin Suit and it also appears the Bank has put the decree into execution though Artha Rin Execution Case No.8 of 2002 from the Court of Artha Rin Adalat No.1 Rangpur. On a persual of the schedule of the complaint it appears accused petitioner mortgaged several acres or land to the Bank. In 1990 BLD (AD) 141 it has been decided that if it is found to be disclosed civil liabilities and for which if complainant has initiated the suit before the Civil Court, the said allegations cannot be brought into a criminal proceeding. We find from the reading of the first information report as well as plaint that the same allegations were made before the criminal Court as well as before the civil Court. Since there is a decree in civil Court as per decisions of 14 DLR (SC) 18 and 51 DLR (AD) 14 where the matter is in seisin of the civil Court, no criminal proceeding can Md Shamsul Hoque, Advocate-For the Petitioner be continued on the said allegations. We find substance in this Rule.
